turns.content: Starting from Planck's spectral radiance per unit wavelength, derive B_lambda(450 nm,T)/B_lambda(700 nm,T) and keep the wavelength prefactor and both dimensionless exponents explicit for T=298 K.
Using hc/k=1.4388e-2 m K, calculate x=hc/(lambda*k*T) for 450 nm and 700 nm at 298 K.
The two exponents are both much larger than one. Apply the corresponding Wien-tail approximation to the exact ratio and reduce it to one evaluable expression.
Use the simplified expression to evaluate the optical refractive index numerically at the stated wavelengths and temperature, and identify which wavelength has the greater spectral output.
Check the result with a logarithmic calculation of the wavelength-prefactor term plus the exponential term, and verify the resulting order of magnitude and wavelength ordering.
Report the final ratio B_lambda(450 nm)/B_lambda(700 nm) and state which wavelength dominates.
